This used to be `this.config?.timeoutMs || FETCH_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`. With `??`, a provider config that has `timeoutMs: 0` now passes `0` to `setTimeout`, and every request aborts with `fetch connect timeout` right away. Keeping `||` for the config fallback avoids that:
```js
const timeoutMs = sanitizedOverride ?? (this.config?.timeoutMs || FETCH_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS);
```

Fixed in b4d9f75 — added `!!` to coerce `reasoning_effort` to a proper boolean:

```js
const hasThinkingMode = !!result.reasoning_effort || result.thinking?.type === "enabled";
```

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Here an unknown seat is ignored and the min is taken over the known seats only, but `comboSeatLimits` in route.js (line 357) sets `contextUnknown` and drops the whole dimension for the same seat. Take a combo of `[known/model-200k, custom/unknown]`: `entry.capabilities.contextWindow` comes out as 200000 while `entry.context_length` is omitted, and a client reading the nested caps gets the exact over-promise the route.js comment says the combo must not make.

I'd pick one rule and use it in both places. Following the route.js reasoning (any seat can serve the request), that means dropping the field once any member is unknown:
```js
const contexts = allCaps.map((c) => c.contextWindow);
const ctxKnown = contexts.every(Number.isFinite);
...(ctxKnown ? { contextWindow: Math.min(...contexts) } : {}),
```
A test that builds one mixed combo and checks that `capabilities.contextWindow` and `context_length` agree would catch any later drift.
